neighbours.label: ' on' / 'mon' in the exasperated interjection 'Come on!' / 'C'mon'
fire: You ate the whole cake by yourself? Come on, that was for the party.
Oh, come on, nobody believes that excuse anymore.
He groaned and said, C'mon, give me a break this time.
Twenty dollars for a coffee? Come on, that's ridiculous.
She laughed and said, oh come on, you're not serious.
Hey, c'mon, ref, that was clearly a handball!
Really? Come on, you promised you'd be here by noon.
Look, come on, guys, we can do much better than this.
quiet: You ate the whole cake by yourself? Wow, that was for the party.
Oh, honestly, nobody believes that excuse anymore.
He groaned and said, please give me a break this time.
Twenty dollars for a coffee? Seriously, that's ridiculous.
The door was unlocked, so we walked right in and sat down.
Please switch on the heater before the guests arrive.
The band will appear on stage at around nine o'clock.
Really? You promised you'd be here by noon.

notes: Probe: interjection Come on 0.86, C'mon 0.76, oh come on 0.58; literal 'come on time' 0.23, 'come on in' 0.10, 'turn on' 0.01. + pole: dismissive commands (shut up, piss off).
